question.problem:
Which of the following statements are true, given that $A$ is a $4\times 4$ matrix and $\text{Null}(A)=\{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ 2{x}_{1} \\ -3{x}_{1} \\ -4{x}_{1}\end{aligned}]\,|\,{x}_{1}\in R\}?$ 

I. $\text{rank}(A)=3$

II. $\text{Col}(A)={R}^{4}$

III. $A$ is not invertible
question.worked_solution:
Since $A$ is a $4\times 4$ matrix, the invertible matrix theorem states the following:

$A$ is invertible $\,⇔\,\{\,\begin{aligned} & \text{Col}(A)={R}^{4} \\  & \text{dim(Col}(A))=4=\text{rank}(A) \\  & \text{Null}(A)=\{0\} \\  & \text{dim(Null}(A))=0=\text{nullity}(A)\end{aligned}$

Also, according to the rank-nullity theorem, if $A$ is a matrix with $n$ columns, then 

$$
\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A)=n.
$$

With that in mind, let's examine each statement in turn.

- Statement I is true. Indeed, since 

$$
\text{Null}(A)=\{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ 2{x}_{1} \\ -3{x}_{1} \\ -4{x}_{1}\end{aligned}]\,|\,{x}_{1}\in R\}=\text{Span}\{\,[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -3 \\ -4\end{aligned}]\}
$$

 
we have that $\text{nullity}(A)=1.$

Now,  for the matrix $A,$ the number of columns is $n=4,$ so according to the rank-nullity theorem, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A) & =n \\ \text{rank}(A)+1 & =4 \\ \text{rank}(A) & =4-1 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement II is false. Since $\text{rank}(A)=3\ne 4,$ then, by the invertible matrix theorem, we have $\text{Col}(A)\ne {R}^{4}.$

- Statement III is true. Indeed, since $\text{rank}(A)=3\ne 4$, according to the  invertible matrix theorem $A$ can't be an invertible matrix.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
